fatal_errors: The proposed SPD treatment does not reconstruct the target intervention: atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating followed by a 550 °C, 2 h anneal.
The study omits the target electrochemical and hot-corrosion conditions, including 3.5 wt% H2SO4 and 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 exposures.
The experiment does not directly distinguish accelerated grain-boundary Cr diffusion from the cited competing explanation of selective Fe dissolution and preferential Cr oxidation.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible, literature-supported alternative hypothesis about ultrafine-grained stainless steel, but it is not a reconstruction of the target coating study. It shares only broad concepts with the target—grain refinement and Cr-enriched passivation—while replacing the HEA coating, annealing schedule, phase structure, environments, and Al/Cr-rich scale mechanism with SPD and grain-boundary Cr transport. The coarse-grained control, electrochemical measurements, XPS, and microscopy provide a reasonable initial study, but SPD also changes residual stress, defect density, texture, and surface reactivity, so the design cannot assign causality specifically to Cr diffusion. A stronger test would include stress-relieved and grain-size-matched controls, time-resolved film chemistry, and a Cr tracer or diffusion-sensitive measurement. The cited review supports improved corrosion and Cr enrichment after SPD, but it explicitly presents more than one possible cause, making the exclusive diffusion claim stronger than the evidence.
